description: CPAT combines the L-method load-flow, Y-method transient-stability and S-method steady-state-stability programs. CRIEPI describes device models informed by its physical power-system simulator and use by Japanese electricity companies and OCCTO. The provider is Central Research Institute of Electric Power Industry. Coverage: The documented application is Japan’s electricity system. Development began in the 1980s, but current release numbers, network limits and simulation intervals are not stated on the page. Access: The institute’s public technical description was read. It does not provide a public software distribution or establish external access conditions. Licence and cost: The page does not establish a reuse licence or complete cost conditions. Provider confirmation is required before reuse. Limitations: The provider’s account of operational use is not an independent performance benchmark. External users must confirm access and applicability. For simulation it provides documented numerical methods for network operation, stability and connection studies. Related resources: The IEEJ standard grid examples are separate benchmark models and do not themselves supply CPAT.
